headlines.title: Constellation Energy And 2 Nuclear Stocks To Watch
headlines.summary: Oil back above US$100 and renewed attacks on energy infrastructure keep reminding markets how fragile fuel supplies can be. That spotlight on energy security is pulling more attention toward nuclear, where output is not tied to shipping lanes or weather. For investors, that creates a clear theme to research. This article walks through three nuclear energy stocks from our screener that aim to tap into that demand.

headlines.title: Why Is Constellation Energy (CEG) Selling Brazos Valley Important For Its Future?
headlines.summary: Constellation Energy (NasdaqGS: CEG) has completed the sale of the Brazos Valley Energy Center to LS Power as part of its Calpine acquisition commitments. The divested Brazos Valley Energy Center is a gas fired generation asset, reducing Constellation's exposure to that specific plant within its overall portfolio. Regulators required the Brazos Valley sale in connection with approving Constellation's purchase of Calpine assets to address competition concerns.

description: Constellation Energy Corporation produces and sells energy products and services in the United States. The company operates through five segments: Mid-Atlantic, Midwest, New York, ERCOT, and Other Power Regions. It offers electricity, natural gas, energy-related products, and sustainable solutions. The company has approximately 31,676 megawatts of generating capacity consisting of nuclear, wind, solar, natural gas, and hydroelectric assets. It serves distribution utilities, municipalities, cooperatives, and commercial, industrial, public sector, and residential customers. The company was incorporated in 2021 and is headquartered in Baltimore, Maryland.
